title: Converge Omnirepo on its Constitution
description:
## Goal

Bring the current 0.8.x implementation into complete alignment with the ratified Omnirepo Constitution and routed Canon architecture.

## Current state

The quality baseline passes, but the implemented product is still a general multi-repository CLI: it creates and clones repositories, runs arbitrary shell commands, accepts ad hoc sync sources, and performs whole-file writes from a central directory list. It does not yet implement constitutional machine/source authority, per-repository applicability and commands, partial managed sections, verified commit/push lifecycle, durable run records, bounded repair, or migration.

## Program rule

Child beads must preserve exact-text synchronization, one-way ordered source authority, independent repository outcomes, complete accounting, and the Boundary 5 repair limit. Every child must add or update tests and pass the repository Canon quality gates.

## Success Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field; every child must close before the epic is eligible.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads are closed; the final implementation passes the Constitution gate across the full product surface; Cargo quality, MSRV, coverage, and pre-commit gates pass; public docs describe only the constitutional product.

title: Remove the arbitrary multi-repository run surface
description:
## Constitutional finding

Boundary 1 says: "Never become a general repository orchestrator." Arbitrary commands are allowed only as repository-declared verification that completes synchronization.

## Current evidence

src/bin/main.rs exposes omnirepo run --command and src/run/runners.rs executes the supplied string through sh -c in every configured directory. tests/cli.rs and src/run/runners_tests.rs currently lock this general orchestration behavior in.

## Scope

Remove the public Run subcommand and the general runner API, tests, and documentation. Preserve command execution only as an internal per-repository verification capability owned by repository configuration and invoked by the synchronization lifecycle.

## Constraints

Do not replace it with another arbitrary fleet command or expose repair as a generic command runner.

## Steps to Reproduce

Configure at least one local repository and run omnirepo run with an arbitrary shell command; the command is accepted and executed in that repository.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: omnirepo help no longer advertises run; invoking run is rejected by clap; no production path accepts a user-supplied shell command for fleet-wide execution; obsolete runner code and tests are removed; future configured verification remains scoped to synchronization; all Canon quality gates pass.

title: Implement verified independent repository lifecycle with commit and push
description:
## Governing contract

Each repository applies synchronization, runs its declared checks, and commits and pushes only after checks pass. Failures do not stop peers. Every repository receives a complete outcome. Omnirepo must never commit or push while configured checks fail.

## Current evidence

Sync currently stops after parallel fs::write and aggregate errors. Run executes arbitrary shell separately. No production path runs per-repo declared checks, stages only current sync changes, commits, pushes, or returns a typed outcome for every fleet member.

## Scope

Create a per-repository state machine for plan application, configured verification, scoped Git staging/commit, and push. Process repositories concurrently, preserve every outcome, and never roll back successful peers. Refuse to include unrelated dirty changes in Omnirepo commits. Classify sync/check/commit/push failures distinctly.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Every machine-declared repository yields one final typed outcome; valid peers finish despite failures; configured checks run after sync; failing checks cause no Omnirepo commit or push; successful changed repos commit only current synchronization/permitted recovery changes and push; unchanged repos avoid empty commits; unrelated dirty files are preserved and excluded; push failure is reported as repository failure; integration tests cover mixed outcomes and nondeterministic completion; all Canon quality gates pass.

title: Write complete durable run summaries with quiet success output
description:
## Governing contract

Quiet success must never cost complete accounting, ordinary Git history, or a durable timestamped record of every fleet run. Canon places summaries under <HOME>/.omnirepo/runs/<timestamp>.log.

## Current evidence

Current operations print progress bars and error tables, return only aggregate Result values, and do not persist run records. Successful per-repository details are mostly optional info logs.

## Scope

Define a stable run/result model and serialize one durable summary for every fleet invocation, including all repository outcomes and collected sync, verification, repair, commit, and push evidence. Keep routine terminal success concise; report named failures and the summary path. Redact secrets while retaining actionable diagnostics.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Every fleet run, including empty, partial, and preflight-failed runs, writes one timestamped summary beneath the canonical home runs directory; every selected repository has a final outcome; failures include stage and bounded command/agent evidence; credentials and tokens are redacted; successful terminal output is concise and failure output names failed repos plus record path; persistence failures affect the command result and are tested; all Canon quality gates pass.

title: Implement separately invoked bounded agent-assisted repair
description:
## Governing contract

Repair is separate from synchronization and may touch destination-local content only to correct a regression caused by the current sync. It may not alter fleet membership, authoritative source content, or source priority. Unrelated or uncertain causation, forbidden action, or exhausted attempts must abort and leave the repository failed.

## Current evidence

There is no production repair operation, agent CLI discovery, configured priority, repair limit, harness integration, causation guard, or re-sync/re-verification loop.

## Scope

Discover supported installed agent CLIs, order them by user configuration, and invoke a separate repair operation only for failed repositories/evidence from the current run. Supply a strict repair prompt and enforce protected paths/authority outside the prompt as well. After each allowed attempt, reapply synchronization and rerun checks before any commit/push. Persist all attempt evidence in the run summary.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Only current-run sync-caused failures are eligible; unrelated or uncertain failures abort without changes; configured tool priority and attempt limits are deterministic; protected machine config and source repositories cannot be changed; each attempt is recorded and followed by sync plus verification; commit/push occurs only after a clean pass; exhausted attempts yield a failed repository while peers remain successful; fake-agent integration tests cover success, refusal, forbidden edits, crashes, and exhaustion; all Canon quality gates pass.

title: Implement explicitly delegated breaking migration operation
description:
## Governing contract

Breaking CLI/config/model releases must identify the break and provide actionable, preferably automated migration guidance. Semantic migration may run only when explicitly delegated and solely to apply the declared Omnirepo migration within the same protected authority boundaries as repair.

## Current evidence

The current project has no migration command, migration manifest/instructions, delegated agent flow, or mechanism connecting releases to repository migration.

## Scope

Define a declared migration artifact and a separately invoked migration operation. Reuse the configured agent selection infrastructure where appropriate, but require explicit user delegation and constrain changes to the named Omnirepo migration. Never use migration for deployment, dependency management, releases, secrets, or unrelated maintenance.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: A breaking release can ship a machine-readable migration declaration plus human instructions; migration never starts implicitly; explicit invocation applies only the selected declared migration to destination repos; machine fleet config, source content, and source priority remain protected; every repo outcome and agent trace is recorded; unrelated changes abort; local fixture tests cover successful, failed, refused, and out-of-scope migrations; all Canon quality gates pass.

title: Align CLI, package metadata, and docs with constitutional synchronization
description:
## Problem

Cargo metadata and README currently describe a general multi-repository manager that creates, clones, and runs commands. The canonical product is authoritative whole-file and partial-section synchronization with independent verified fleet convergence.

## Scope

Rewrite CLI help, README, examples, package description/keywords, and configuration examples after the core behavior lands. Document machine/source/repository authority, inference versus explicit policy, all/allow/exclude scope, exact overwrite semantics, partial tags by format, verification, independent outcomes, Git behavior, run records, repair boundaries, and explicit breaking migration from 0.8.x.

## Constraints

Do not promise formats, limits, retries, auth behavior, or migration mechanics that the implementation and Canon do not own.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: All public wording describes synchronization rather than general orchestration; obsolete new/run and legacy .omni.yaml examples are gone; setup reaches a first inferred sync with minimal config; partial delimiter examples match implementation; failure/repair/Git/run-record behavior is accurate; 0.8.x breaking changes have actionable and preferably automated migration instructions; CLI snapshots/integration tests cover help and errors; all Canon quality gates pass.

title: Remove the legacy tag-based clone workflow
description:
## Constitutional finding

Machine configuration alone owns destination fleet membership and ordered source repositories. Repository applicability belongs to repository policy. Growth must remain focused on synchronization rather than general repository orchestration.

## Current evidence

src/bin/main.rs exposes clone --tags. src/clone/repository_clone.rs selects repository URLs/destinations by tags, clones them in parallel, and writes a central .omni.yaml dirs list. This legacy flow conflates fleet setup, applicability, and working-directory state.

## Scope

Remove the public tag-based clone workflow and its .omni.yaml generation. If source-repository materialization is needed by the ordered-source implementation, keep it as an internal machine-config-driven synchronization prerequisite with no tag heuristics and no destination-to-source flow. Do not invent automatic destination cloning policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The public CLI no longer exposes tag-based fleet cloning; .omni.yaml is not generated; tag matching does not determine fleet membership or sync applicability; any retained Git clone code is internal, driven solely by machine-declared source repositories, preserves configured order, and cannot clone or modify undeclared destinations; obsolete tests/docs are removed or replaced; all Canon quality gates pass.

title: Define source-repository materialization policy
description:
## Policy gap

The Constitution and Canon establish that ordered source repositories are authoritative, but they do not define how a machine-config source entry is represented or materialized.

## Human input required

The owner must explicitly choose supported source references such as local paths and/or Git URLs; checkout/cache location; refresh behavior per run; dirty-source handling; authentication source; timeout; retry/backoff; and offline behavior. Current HTTP template and git clone mechanisms are not constitutional authority for these choices.

## Constraint

No implementation may infer these policies from reqwest, Git, the current tag-based clone command, or ambient machine behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner explicitly selects the supported source reference forms and lifecycle policies; the smallest owning Canon page records the resulting durable guarantees and precedence; the source-declaration bead is updated with the decided contract and can proceed without guessed transport, auth, timeout, retry, cache, or dirty-state behavior.

title: Define ownership and precedence for fleet execution controls
description:
## Policy gap

The owner has required configurable fleet parallelism, agent priority, repair limits, and harness options. Canon assigns machine configuration to fleet/source authority and repository configuration to applicability/commands, but does not assign these operational controls or their precedence.

## Human input required

The owner must place each control in a configuration tier and state override precedence, including whether CLI overrides exist. Repository policy must not gain authority over fleet membership, authoritative sources, or source priority.

## Constraint

No implementation may guess a global-versus-repository ownership model from current Rayon defaults or legacy CLI flags.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The owner explicitly assigns fleet parallelism, agent discovery priority, repair-attempt limits, and harness settings to configuration tiers and defines precedence; the owning Canon page records the durable rule; lifecycle and repair beads are updated with the selected schema and can proceed without guessing.

title: Retire general-purpose repository creation
description:
## Constitutional finding

Growth Directive 5 says to grow through file and section synchronization, "not by expanding into general repository orchestration." Boundary 1 limits Omnirepo to synchronization plus commit, push, checks, and sync-induced repair.

## Current evidence

src/bin/main.rs exposes new; src/new/project_creation.rs creates arbitrary repositories, copies tag-selected templates, and runs git init. README.md presents repository creation as a core product feature.

## Scope

Remove the general new command and its production module, tests, and documentation. Any future onboarding must be a synchronization-specific setup path driven by the constitutional configuration and inference model, not a generic project generator.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: The public CLI has no general new command; project creation/template-generation code and obsolete tests are removed; README and package wording no longer claim general project generation; installation-to-first-sync onboarding remains covered by the configuration/inference beads; all Canon quality gates pass.

title: Implement canonical machine and repository configuration authority
description:
## Governing contract

Convention governs until intent is declared. Machine configuration alone owns fleet membership, ordered authoritative sources, and source priority. A root .omnirepo.<ext> owns only that destination repository's all, allow, exclude, and verification-command policy.

## Current evidence

src/config/parser.rs models repositories and templates plus a central RepoConfig containing only dirs. src/util/utilities.rs searches ~/.omnirepo.yaml and ~/.omnirepo/.omnirepo.yaml. Clone, run, and sync use a working-directory .omni.yaml instead of per-repository policy.

## Scope

Introduce typed machine configuration at <HOME>/.omnirepo/config.<ext> and typed root repository configuration at .omnirepo.<ext>. Keep fleet/source authority out of destination policy. Validate unknown, conflicting, and malformed applicability controls with contextual errors. Preserve ordered source entries exactly.

## Compatibility

This is an explicit breaking configuration change and must feed the migration/documentation bead.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Machine config loads from the canonical home location and contains destination fleet entries plus ordered source repositories; repository config contains all/allow/exclude controls and verification commands only; repository config cannot redefine fleet or source priority; presence of repository config disables inference; parsing, precedence, invalid-case, and round-trip tests exist; old .omni.yaml is not silently treated as the new policy; all Canon quality gates pass.

title: Load source-repository declarations with deterministic precedence
description:
## Governing contract

Authority flows one way from ordered source repositories to destinations. Source repositories declare the files and sections they provide. When declarations overlap, configured source order is the sole tiebreaker.

## Current evidence

The current sync command accepts an arbitrary URL, template ID, or local file. Config templates are remote file URLs, and no source-repository declaration model exists. A local file under the destination root can currently become the source for peers.

## Scope

Define and load source-side declarations for whole files and managed sections. Resolve overlapping declarations only by machine-config source order. Build a source catalog without examining destination content for authority. Reject attempts to promote destination files or CLI ad hoc sources.

## Open implementation edge

Source checkout/update transport must remain isolated behind an interface and must not invent unrecorded auth, retry, or cache policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Local fixture source repositories can declare whole files and sections; catalog order is stable and follows machine configuration; overlap resolution is deterministic and independent of completion/content; destinations and CLI arguments cannot become authoritative sources; duplicate/invalid declarations fail contextually; tests cover overlap, ordering, one-way authority, and invalid declarations; all Canon quality gates pass.

title: Build per-repository synchronization plans with explicit scope and inference
description:
## Governing contract

A repository without configuration receives useful inferred synchronization. Once repository configuration exists, it wholly governs all, allow, exclude, and command scope. Inference may never overrule declared intent.

## Current evidence

Current sync reads one central .omni.yaml dirs list and writes one CLI-selected filename to every listed repository. There is no per-repository applicability plan or source-declaration matching.

## Scope

For every machine-declared destination, combine the ordered source catalog with that repository's policy to produce an explicit immutable sync plan. No-config repositories receive all applicable inferred declarations. Configured repositories receive exactly the all/allow/exclude result, including supported combinations. Record why each item is included or excluded for diagnostics without changing precedence.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Plans are produced only for machine-declared fleet repositories; absent repository config infers every applicable declaration; present config wholly determines scope; allow/exclude/all combinations have deterministic semantics; exclusions cannot be reintroduced by inference; plan ordering follows source precedence; table/property tests cover configured and unconfigured repositories, overlaps, empty plans, and invalid selectors; all Canon quality gates pass.

title: Implement idempotent exact whole-file synchronization
description:
## Governing contract

Managed means authoritative and exact text outranks semantic cleverness. A whole managed file is replaced from its authoritative source without preserving local drift or parsing its format.

## Current evidence

src/sync/synchronization.rs already writes the same in-memory String with fs::write, but it is driven by ad hoc source selection and a central dirs file, performs no explicit equality check, and is not integrated with per-repository plans or lifecycle outcomes.

## Scope

Implement a managed-content operation over a resolved plan entry. Compare exact bytes/text, report unchanged versus changed, create missing parent directories, and replace a differing whole file faithfully. Do not normalize newlines, reorder data, or invoke semantic editors. Produce structured per-repository results for the lifecycle.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Missing whole files are created exactly; drifted files are overwritten exactly; already-equal files are reported unchanged without a content rewrite; newline and Unicode cases preserve source text; no format parser changes managed content; failures leave a structured repository/item outcome; tests include pre-existing drift, empty files, equality, nested paths, and partial fleet failure; all Canon quality gates pass.

title: Implement managed partial sections and delimiter knowledge
description:
## Governing contract

A managed section gives authority only between one start/end delimiter pair expressed as valid comments for the file format. Outside content is preserved. An absent section is appended with both delimiters. Unmatched, reversed, duplicate, or nested delimiters fail without changing the file.

## Current evidence

No delimiter, file-format, section, or partial-update code exists. Current sync always replaces the complete target through fs::write.

## Scope

Add a small comment-syntax knowledge base for common configuration formats solely to render Omnirepo delimiters. Implement exact section matching, replacement, append-on-absence, and ambiguity detection. Treat the section body as exact text and never parse the surrounding configuration semantically.

## Documentation

Document the literal tags users place in each supported file format.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Each supported format has tested valid comment delimiters; exactly one ordered non-nested pair is replaced while all outside text remains byte-for-byte unchanged; missing sections append one canonical delimited section; unmatched, reversed, duplicate, and nested delimiters return errors and leave files unchanged; unknown format errors rather than guessing syntax; property tests exercise outside-content preservation; all Canon quality gates pass.

title: Enforce symlink-safe containment within the declared fleet
description:
## Governing contract

Unattended convergence must never change repositories outside the machine-declared fleet. The sync engine may never cross managed partial delimiters.

## Current evidence

src/util/utilities.rs rejects lexical absolute paths and parent components, but later fs::metadata, create_dir_all, and fs::write calls follow symlinks. A repository root or target component can therefore escape the selected destination tree despite lexical checks.

## Scope

Resolve and validate machine-declared repository roots and every managed target with symlink-aware containment before mutation. Protect source reads, destination writes, Git working directories, and config discovery. Handle non-existent leaf paths without weakening containment. Preserve independent outcomes so one rejected repo does not stop valid peers.

## Steps to Reproduce

Place a symlink inside a lexically valid declared repository path that points outside the fleet, then synchronize a managed target through that symlink; current filesystem writes follow the link.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Absolute/traversal and symlink escapes are rejected before mutation; nested symlinks cannot redirect managed writes, source reads, verification, commit, or push outside allowed roots; legitimate nested paths still work; TOCTOU limitations are documented and minimized with the chosen filesystem approach; integration tests cover root and leaf symlink escapes plus valid peers; all Canon quality gates pass.

title: Build a hermetic fleet lifecycle integration-test harness
description:
## Purpose

The remaining constitutional lifecycle requires repeatable tests across multiple repositories, Git remotes, verification commands, failures, and agent CLIs.

## Current evidence

The current suite has strong unit coverage and 19 CLI tests, but no reusable end-to-end harness for source repositories, destination repositories with bare remotes, push assertions, lifecycle run records, repair attempts, or agent discovery.

## Scope

Create test fixtures that provision local source repos, destination repos, bare remotes, deterministic Git identity, repository configs, fake verification commands, fake agent CLIs, and isolated HOME/PATH. No external network or ambient user Git configuration may affect the tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

See the structured acceptance criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: Tests can create multi-repo fleets with local remotes and assert exact commits/pushes; fake checks and agents capture arguments/stdin/stdout/stderr and deterministic exit states; HOME, PATH, Git config, and run-record locations are isolated; fixtures support success, partial failure, retry, timeout, and no-op cases; CI and MSRV remain supported; all Canon quality gates pass.
